scenarios.name: Arm 1 — ROLLBACK_POPULATIONS: FileCas / MintedSet / DoorGuard, one JSON document per cell
scenarios.detail:
Repro (all three cells, rig-built corpora, binary /Users/maurice/projects/gherrink-jigc/target/debug/jigc @ 26d021de, 1.0.0-rc.15):

FileCas — `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; install a pre-commit hook that appends `RACER LINE` to docs/milestone-records/*.md and exits 1; `jigc milestone create "Cache rework" --format json`.
Observed: exit 1; stdout 0 bytes; stderr ONE parseable document carrying `milestone-create.commit-rejected` (key target `milestone:cache-rework`) AND `milestone.rollback-conflict` (key target `docs/milestone-records/cache-rework.md`). `grep -rn 'RACER LINE' docs/` -> `docs/milestone-records/cache-rework.md:10:RACER LINE` — the racer's bytes survived.
Same at `jigc rename adr:alpha-call --to 'Beta Call' --slug beta-call --format json` under a hook writing at the new path: exit 1, `rename.commit-rejected` + `rename.rollback-conflict`, `docs/decisions/beta-call.md` still carries `RACER AT NEW PATH`.
Same at `jigc task finalize <id> --format json` under a hook writing at the promoted path: exit 1, `finalize.commit-rejected` + `finalize.rollback-conflict`, `docs/decisions/gamma-call.md` still carries `RACER AT PROMOTED PATH`.

MintedSet — hook plants into the minted area and exits 1; `jigc milestone create "Index rework" --format json` -> `milestone.foreign-bytes` target `.jigc/milestones/index-rework`, and `.jigc/milestones/index-rework/FOREIGN-SCRATCH.txt` survives. `jigc milestone add-task wave-one 'sub one' --workflow dev-task --format json` with the hook planting `.jigc/tasks/*/docs/RACER.md` -> `milestone.foreign-bytes` target `.jigc/tasks/sub-one`, and `.jigc/tasks/sub-one/docs/RACER.md` still reads `THIRD PARTY PROSE`.

DoorGuard — `printf 'MY OWN EDIT\n' >> .jigc/AGENT.md; jigc setup --format json` -> exit 1, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 1029 bytes = one document carrying `setup.dirty-install-path` on the FINDINGS arm (Increment 1's D6 move), and `diff` of the pre-run copy against `.jigc/AGENT.md` is IDENTICAL — refused before the first write.

Stream discipline held at every driven reject: stdout 0 bytes, stderr exactly one JSON value.

scenarios.name: Arm 2 — InProgress::ALL x acting doors: refusal, and the emitted route run through a real shell
scenarios.detail:
Repro: for st in merge squash-merge rebase-merge rebase-apply am cherry-pick sequencer dangling-sequencer revert unmerged-index bisect detached; do `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig fresh --git-state $st) || exit; eval "$rig"`; `jigc milestone create probe`; lift each `git …` token out of the printed route and run it; re-probe. done

Observed: all 12 states exit 1. Nouns/routes: merge -> `git merge --continue`/`--abort`; squash-merge -> 'a squash merge is staged and not committed' route `git reset --merge`; rebase-merge & rebase-apply -> `git rebase --continue`/`--abort`; am -> 'a `git am` is in progress' route `git am --continue`/`git am --abort` (NOT `git rebase --abort`); cherry-pick & sequencer -> `git cherry-pick --continue`/`--abort`; dangling-sequencer -> 'left a queue of commits in `sequencer/`' route `git cherry-pick --quit`; revert -> `git revert --continue`/`--abort`; unmerged-index (NO marker) -> 'a conflict left unmerged paths in the index' route `git reset --merge`; bisect -> `git bisect reset`; detached -> `repo.head-detached` route `git switch <branch>`.
Every abandon route run through zsh returned git exit 0 and left NO operation marker; the same door then succeeded (exit 0). `--continue` routes return 128/1 as expected (they are conditioned on 'once its conflicts are resolved').

Across doors in ONE mid-revert repo (`dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons --git-state revert`): `jigc milestone create` exit 1, `jigc rename vision:vision --to 'New Vision'` exit 1, `jigc task validate probe-task` exit 1, `jigc task finalize probe-task` exit 1 — all the SAME finding and route; `jigc task validate` previews exactly what `finalize` prints. Move-on-behalf mid-merge: `jigc config set docs-root papers` exit 1, `jigc config set placement-root sub` exit 1. Controls silent: `jigc describe` exit 0, `jigc doc show vision` exit 0, `jigc doc list` exit 0, `jigc validate` exit 0. REVERT_HEAD/MERGE_MSG untouched by every refusal.

scenarios.name: Arm 3 — the destroying subject: Refuse / Narrate / Displace, collision-safety, zero false fire
scenarios.detail:
Repro: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons --start dev-task 'add a widget') || exit; eval "$rig"`; plant into .jigc/tasks/add-a-widget/: NOTES.md, analysis/perf.txt (nested dir), docs/notes.txt (non-.md under docs/), .secret (dotfile), link-to-hosts (symlink -> /etc/hosts).

Refuse: `jigc task discard add-a-widget` -> exit 1, `task-discard.foreign-bytes` naming ALL FIVE paths, route naming `--force`; `find .jigc/tasks/add-a-widget` afterwards shows every planted path still present and every jigc file untouched.
Narrate: second task, plant KEEP.md + sub/deep.txt, `jigc task discard second-probe --force` -> exit 0, warning naming both paths plus 'the working area is the only copy of these bytes', area removed.
Displace: fill the commit doc, `jigc task finalize add-a-widget --format json` -> exit 0, stdout one document whose `committed.displaced` lists all five {from,to} pairs, stderr carrying the same five as a loss-shaped side channel. `find .jigc/displaced` shows .jigc/displaced/add-a-widget/{.secret,NOTES.md,analysis/perf.txt,docs/notes.txt,link-to-hosts} with relative paths preserved; contents byte-identical; `ls -l` confirms the symlink is still a symlink -> /etc/hosts.
docs/*.md-that-is-no-staged-identity cell: `printf '# Bogus\n' > .jigc/tasks/third-probe/docs/bogus.md; jigc task finalize third-probe` -> exit 3 `schema-conformance.unknown-type` with a route — answered by the gate before any teardown, exactly as the chapter records.
Collision safety (my own probe, not in the walk): run the same task id twice, each planting a DIFFERENT NOTES.md. Run 1 -> .jigc/displaced/same-id/NOTES.md ('FIRST AGENT PROSE — irreplaceable'); run 2 -> .jigc/displaced/same-id/NOTES.md.2 ('SECOND AGENT PROSE'). The first agent's bytes are NOT clobbered.
Zero false fire: `jigc start --workflow record-decision` -> `jigc doc create adr --title 'First Decision' --task T` -> `jigc doc rename adr:first-decision --to 'First Call' --task T` (writes renames.json + roles.json) -> `jigc task validate T` -> `jigc task discard T` refuses with `task-discard.staged-prose`, NOT foreign-bytes. jigc's own files are never called foreign.
Other destroying doors: `jigc milestone discard discard-probe` over .jigc/milestones/discard-probe/FOREIGN.txt -> exit 1 `milestone.foreign-bytes`, file survives. `jigc milestone provision` over .jigc/worktrees/one/LEFT.txt -> exit 1 `milestone.leftover-holds-work`, file survives. `jigc uninstall --format json` over .jigc/displaced/x/keep.md -> exit 1 `uninstall.foreign-bytes` on the findings arm (stdout 0 bytes), file survives.

scenarios.name: Arm 4a — migrate-corpus sees and lands a doc whose home moved, and the read surface follows it
scenarios.detail:
Repro: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig fresh --pack-from-dev --repin) || exit; eval "$rig"`; commit a conformant `CHANGELOG.md` (schema-version: 2) and `jigc ingest`; then manufacture a placement->location home move at v3 in the throwaway pack: `cp $RIG/pack/schemas/changelog.yaml $RIG/pack/schema-snapshots/changelog.v2.yaml`; `sed -i '' 's|^placement: { file: CHANGELOG.md }$|location: history|' $RIG/pack/schemas/changelog.yaml`; bump the manifest entry to `schema-version: 3` and re-pin its `schema-hash` from the loader's own 'recomputed' line.

Observed: `jigc migrate-corpus` -> exit 0, `corpus migration: 1 migrated, 0 already current, 0 blocked` / `migrated docs/history/changelog.md`, `committed fa2f089 — only the migrated paths were staged`. `head -3 docs/history/changelog.md` shows `schema-version: 3`; the authored prose is byte-preserved; the prior home is empty. `jigc validate` exit 0. `jigc doc list` -> `changelog:changelog  docs/history/changelog.md  managed`. `jigc doc show changelog --format json` exit 0 returning the document at the NEW home — the adopter's done picture, not just a migration report.

scenarios.name: Arm 4b — schema-conformance.home-vacated on the fresh-clone shape
scenarios.detail:
Repro: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; `git mv CHANGELOG.md HISTORY.md && git commit -q --no-verify -m 'move changelog'`; `git clone "$REPO" $(mktemp -d)/c`; cd into the clone; `jigc validate`.

Observed: exit 1 with `blocking · schema-conformance.home-vacated — \`changelog\` homes its one document at \`CHANGELOG.md\`, the repository's history touches that path, and nothing is there now`, `at: CHANGELOG.md`, route naming `git log --diff-filter=D -1 -- CHANGELOG.md` and `jigc ingest`, plus the exit-flip trailer. The gitignored file-state cache is absent in the clone, so the finding survives a clone as designed. Control: on a `dev/jigc-rig fresh` corpus where the file never existed, `jigc validate` exits 0 and says nothing about home-vacated.

scenarios.name: Arm 4c — jigc validate FALSE-GREENS over a below-version doc stranded at a vacated repo-root prior home (FINDING 1)
scenarios.detail:
FINDING 1 — HIGH. After a schema bump that ALSO moves a doctype's home off a repo-root placement file, `jigc validate` prints 'no findings — the committed store validates clean' at exit 0 over an unmigrated managed corpus, and `jigc doc list` reports 'no committed docs' — while `jigc migrate-corpus` sees the very same doc. This is the M42 false-green class (`schema-conformance.schema-version-current`, a STORE_EXIT_FLIPS member built precisely so validate exits non-zero over an unmigrated managed corpus) reopened through an axis Increment 7 widened on the migrate side only.

EXACT REPRO (paste-runnable from the repo root; binary target/debug/jigc @ 26d021de, 1.0.0-rc.15):
  rig=$(dev/jigc-rig fresh --pack-from-dev --repin) || exit; eval "$rig"; P=$RIG
  printf -- '---\nschema-version: 2\n---\n\n# Changelog\n\n## Unreleased Changes\n\n### changed  {#changed}\n\n- prose a human wrote\n\n\n## Releases\n\n' > CHANGELOG.md
  git add CHANGELOG.md && git commit -q --no-verify -m 'add changelog'; "$JIGC" ingest >/dev/null
  cp "$P/pack/schemas/changelog.yaml" "$P/pack/schema-snapshots/changelog.v2.yaml"
  sed -i '' 's|^placement: { file: CHANGELOG.md }$|location: history|' "$P/pack/schemas/changelog.yaml"
  sed -i '' '/- type: changelog/,/schema-hash:/ s/schema-version: 2/schema-version: 3/' "$P/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml"
  h=$("$JIGC" doc list 2>&1 | sed -n 's/.*recomputed `\([0-9a-f]*\)`.*/\1/p'); old=$(grep -A2 'type: changelog' "$P/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml" | sed -n 's/.*schema-hash: //p'); sed -i '' "s/$old/$h/" "$P/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml"
  "$JIGC" doc list; "$JIGC" validate; echo "validate exit=$?"; "$JIGC" migrate-corpus --dry-run

OBSERVED:
  $ jigc doc list
  jigc doc list — no committed docs          <-- the managed doc is INVISIBLE to the pinned index read
  $ jigc validate
  no findings — the committed store validates clean
  validate exit=0                            <-- FALSE GREEN over an unmigrated managed corpus
  $ head -2 CHANGELOG.md  ->  ---  /  schema-version: 2   (still on disk, stamped below current 3)
  $ jigc migrate-corpus --dry-run
  corpus migration (dry run …): 1 would migrate, 0 already current, 0 blocked
    would migrate docs/history/changelog.md   <-- the tool KNOWS the doc is there and below-version

CONTROL (proves the fence works when the home did NOT move): same rig, an `adr` stamped v1 while current is v2, sitting at its current home -> `jigc validate` exit 1 with `schema-conformance.schema-version-current — docs/decisions/first-call.md: field schema-version is schema-version 1, below the current schema-version 2` plus the exit-flip trailer.

CONTROL (bounds the class): the SAME manufactured bump on `adr` (location decisions/ -> decisions2/, both inside docs-root, i.e. inside `orphan::Territory`) is NOT silent — `jigc validate` exits 1 with `schema-conformance.orphaned-instance` and `jigc doc list` prints the row as `orphaned`. So the silence is specific to prior homes OUTSIDE Territory.

HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: `orphan::Territory` is the resolved docs-root tree ∪ a non-repo-root `placement-root` ∪ every resolved doctype's home DIRECTORY; design/validation.md:712 states the repo root is deliberately excluded ('a repo-root home declares no directory that is not the whole repository'). Membership therefore = doctypes whose PRIOR declared home is a repo-root file. `grep -rn '^placement:' crates/cli/pack/schemas/ packs/methodology/schemas/` -> 5 placement doctypes, of which 2 home at the repo root (`changelog` -> CHANGELOG.md, `vision` -> VISION.md). The general statement of the class, which I did NOT enumerate consumers for and therefore label unbounded: wherever `migrate-corpus`'s prior-home walk can see a below-version doc that the store-scope conformance sweep's candidate enumeration cannot, `validate` false-greens — two enumerations that must agree and do not.

WHY IT IS NOT THE DECLARED RESIDUAL: design/validation.md:712 declares an open residual for a DEPARTED doctype ('once the pack that declared the type leaves the composition there is no resolved home left to read'). That does not describe this cell — `changelog` still resolves, its home is readable, the snapshot store names the prior home, and `migrate-corpus` uses it. This is a sibling of the declared residual through an un-swept axis, and it lands on the verb MIGRATING.md tells adopters to gate on ('Ask `jigc validate` whether you need to migrate — it blocks if you do').

scenarios.name: Arm 5 — the fixed-identity doctype set x the address-door registry, and the contract-version 7 projection
scenarios.detail:
Repro: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; `jigc doc schema <ty> --format json` for all 16 doctypes of both packs; then `jigc start --workflow dev-task 'identity probe'` and drive every address door with `<ty>:bogus`.

Projection: all 16 doctypes return `"contract-version": 7` with `identity: {kind, address}` and `home: {kind, path}` — e.g. changelog {fixed, 'changelog'} / {placement, 'CHANGELOG.md'}; vision {fixed, 'vision'} / {placement, 'VISION.md'}; adr {slugged, 'adr:<slug>'} / {location, 'docs/decisions/<slug>.md'}; commit {slugged} / {transient, null}. The DERIVED fixed-identity set is exactly {changelog, decisions-log, deferral-ledger, roadmap, vision} — which matches the independent grep of `^placement:` across both packs.

Doors: for each of those 5 doctypes, all of `doc show`, `doc set-field`, `doc set-slot`, `doc add-item`, `doc retitle-item`, `doc rename`, `rename`, `milestone add-from-spec` exit 1 with `store.fixed-identity`, route `jigc doc show <ty>:<ty>`. Example: `jigc doc show vision:bogus` -> 'blocking · store.fixed-identity — `vision:bogus` is not an address `vision` can have: its identity is fixed … so `vision:vision` is the one instance this doctype has'.
`jigc rename changelog:changelog --to 'Axis' --slug bogus` -> exit 1 `write.identity-change`, route `jigc rename changelog:changelog --to Axis --slug changelog` — the route no longer composes the caller's token; `git status --short` empty and CHANGELOG.md untouched.
OS name ceiling at the address head: `printf 'x' | jigc doc set-slot "vision:$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..300})#thesis" --from-file -` -> exit 1 `write.slug-name-ceiling — … is 300 bytes — over the 165-byte ceiling a doc identity carries`.
Stated cells behave as stated: `jigc task bind spec vision:bogus <task>` resolves the ROLE first ('role `spec` is not a declared read-role of this task'); `jigc doc author` takes a doctype, not an address, so it is not an Address door (control `adr:whatever` gives the same `create.unknown-doctype`).
Root knobs: `jigc config set docs-root .jigc` exit 1; `jigc config set placement-root <300xa>` exit 1 `config.unusable-root`; `''` and `x/../y` are ACCEPTED with explicit acks ('you typed an empty value, which names the repository root `.`' / 'you typed `x/../y`, which folds to `y`'), and `jigc config get placement-root` confirms the folded value, with the stranded docs relocated and named.

scenarios.name: Arm 6 — pre-dispatch faults x every clap leaf, not-set-up at every milestone leaf, and the emitted route run
scenarios.detail:
Deleted cwd: `D=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $D/inner; cd $D/inner; rmdir $D/inner`; then 41 leaf invocations with `--format json` (start, workflow, all 12 doc leaves, 6 task leaves, 3 config leaves, all 9 milestone leaves, setup, uninstall, upgrade, ingest, migrate, migrate-corpus, unmanage, rename, relocate, describe, validate). Observed: 40/41 exit 1 and emit EXACTLY ONE parseable JSON document (checked with json.loads over the merged streams). The one exception is `doc author` with a missing required `--from-file`, which is a clap usage error at exit 2 — declared out of the fault registry.

Malformed packs.yaml: `cat > .jigc/config/packs.yaml <<'EOF'\npacks: [ this is : not : valid yaml\nEOF`; every leaf answers one document — e.g. `jigc validate --format json` -> stdout 0 bytes, stderr `{"error": ".jigc/config/packs.yaml is not a valid pack-set list: packs[0]: invalid type: map, expected path string at line 1 column 10"}`. `jigc task list --format json` exits 0 with `[]`, consistent with its declared top-level-array arm and its out-of-phase relation (it loads no packs).

Not-set-up (Increment 8's rider): `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig bare) || exit; eval "$rig"`; all NINE milestone leaves (create, add-task, add-from-spec, list-tasks, provision, execute, join, finalize, discard) exit 1 with the flattened `{error}` arm `"this project isn't set up — run \`jigc setup\` (no \`.jigc/config/\` cascade layer found)"`, and `ls .jigc` afterwards -> 'No such file or directory' — nothing written.

The driven route half: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; `printf '# My Notes\n\nSome prose.\n' > 'my notes.md'`; `jigc migrate 'my notes.md' --as adr` -> exit 1 `migrate.source-untracked`, route ``stage it with `git add -- 'my notes.md'` ``. Lifting that route out of the printed bytes and running it through zsh: git exit 0, `git status --short` -> `A  "my notes.md"`. The re-run line lifted the same way (`jigc migrate 'my notes.md' --as adr`) then exits 0 and mints `migrate-adr-my-notes-fed83034187c`.

scenarios.name: Arm 7 — the verb-routed workflow set x both compose doors, plus the empty case and the exit-4 seam
scenarios.detail:
Set derived from both packs: `grep -rln 'suppressed:' crates/cli/pack/workflows packs/methodology/workflows` and reading each `door:` -> 14 members carry a door (sub-task, milestone-execution, and the 12 migrate-*), 8 suppressed workflows carry none.

Repro: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; for each of the 14: `jigc start --workflow <w> probe` and `jigc workflow <w> --preview`.
Observed: 14/14 x 2 doors -> exit 1 with `workflow.verb-routed`; `jigc task list` afterwards -> 'no active tasks' (nothing minted at either door). Example: `jigc start --workflow migrate-adr probe` -> route ``jigc migrate <path> --as adr``.
Control: `jigc workflow single-task --preview` exit 0 and `jigc start --workflow single-task 'control probe'` exit 0.
Empty enumeration: `jigc workflow implement-from-spec --preview` over a spec-less corpus composes '(nothing is listed until a `spec` is committed; with none there is nothing to bind here — author one first through the `plan` workflow, then start this work again)'.
Exit-4 seam through the project cascade layer: write `.jigc/config/workflows/quick-fix.yaml` with a migrate-shaped body (`{{ include: step:author-migration-adr }}` + `{{ include: step:migration-finalize }}`) and no suppression; `jigc start --workflow quick-fix 'off-verb migrate shape'` mints; fill the commit doc; `jigc task finalize off-verb-migrate-shape` -> exit 4, 'migration review required — nothing committed … no foreign source was staged for it', and HEAD is byte-identical before and after (52309647… both sides).
Increment 10's catalog fix: a project shadow of `quick-fix` carrying `selectable: false` + `suppressed.door` is NOT listed by `jigc start` (grep for quick-fix in the catalog returns nothing), `jigc describe --workflows` says 'It is hidden from the router catalog: verb-routed…', and `jigc start --workflow quick-fix` exits 1 with `workflow.verb-routed` and the door as route — the three surfaces agree.

scenarios.name: Fan-out — N-process binary sim through the VERBATIM rendered spawn template, three divergent orders, byte-identical output
scenarios.detail:
Three independent rigs, one per execution order (id-order 'fwd', reverse 'rev', middle-out 'mid'), each: `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; `jigc config set finalize.fan-out.squash false`; `jigc milestone create 'Alpha Wave'`; three `jigc milestone add-task alpha-wave 'task <charlie|bravo|alpha>' --workflow dev-task` (deliberately added in REVERSE id order); `jigc milestone list-tasks alpha-wave` -> `task-alpha, task-bravo, task-charlie` (canonical id-sorted, independent of add order); `jigc milestone provision alpha-wave`.

The spawn template was RENDERED THROUGH THE BINARY and executed verbatim: `jigc milestone execute alpha-wave` emits
  Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/task-alpha && jigc workflow dev-task --task task-alpha`
  Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/task-bravo && jigc workflow dev-task --task task-bravo`
  Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/task-charlie && jigc workflow dev-task --task task-charlie`
Each line was lifted out of those bytes, had only the bare word `jigc` resolved to the built binary, and was run as its OWN process through a real shell — re-entry exit 0 for all three in every order. (The template names each sub-task's RECORDED workflow, `dev-task`, not a fixed `sub-task` — M49's fix; a hand-written `jigc workflow sub-task --task <id>` fails with exit 1, so the verbatim render is what works.)

Then per order: write one code file in each worktree + `git add`, author each commit doc through `jigc doc set-field`/`set-slot --task <id>`, `jigc milestone join alpha-wave` (exit 0), `jigc milestone finalize alpha-wave --format json` (exit 0).

ORDER-INVARIANCE ASSERTION: `git ls-tree -r HEAD | sort` compared across all three runs is IDENTICAL except for a single blob, `docs/milestone-records/alpha-wave.md`, whose only differing line is `base: <sha> <short>` — the repo-unique base pin, which differs because the three rigs are three separately constructed repositories, not because of execution order. `git log --format='%B' -5 | shasum` is byte-identical across all three: ac19487a5ee05cfdfb23063317a3ed88e14666c6. Commit subjects appear in id order in all three (`feat(core): add task-alpha` / `task-bravo` / `task-charlie`), never in execution order.

HONEST BOUND: this is the N-PROCESS BINARY SIM plus the verbatim spawn-template execution. The genuine concurrent assistant Task-tool spawn is the ORCHESTRATOR'S MAIN-SESSION half and I did NOT run it — I am headless and cannot spawn the assistant's Task tool. Do not read this green as the real-spawn proof.

scenarios.name: Milestone-boundary displacement (Increment 4 amendment §18: milestone finalize is the fifth destroying door)
scenarios.detail:
Repro: in the fan-out run above, before `jigc milestone join`, plant `printf 'sub-agent scratch\n' > .jigc/tasks/task-alpha/BOUNDARY-NOTES.md`; then `jigc milestone finalize alpha-wave --format json`.

scenarios.name: Misuse sweep off the done-picture path (undeclared addresses, reserved depth, degenerate ids, non-git)
scenarios.detail:
Repro (rig `committed-singletons` with an open task): 
`jigc doc set-slot changelog:changelog#nosuch --task probe --from-file /dev/null` -> `write.unknown-section`, route `jigc doc schema changelog`.
`jigc doc set-field changelog:changelog#unreleased-changes/nosuch --value x` -> `write.unknown-field`.
`jigc doc set-slot 'changelog:changelog#releases/1-0-0/changes/added/nosuch'` -> `write.unknown-field` naming the nested item ('no slot "nosuch" declared on item "1-0-0/changes/added" in section "releases"') — the nested hop resolves.
`jigc doc retitle-item 'changelog:changelog#unreleased-changes/nope'` -> `write.not-present`, route `jigc doc show changelog:changelog#unreleased-changes --task probe`.
Reserved-depth (M49/M45 class), driven at a NESTED item slot: `printf '#### fake-group\n\n- x\n' | jigc doc set-slot 'changelog:changelog#releases/1-0-0/changes/added/notes' --task probe --from-file -` -> exit 1 `write.slot-heading-depth — heading at schema-reserved depth \`####\` … \`#####\` is the shallowest depth free at this address`; `###` likewise refused; `#####` accepted and round-trips byte-faithfully through `jigc doc show … --format json`. At the SINGLE-level section `unreleased-changes` (which declares no nested group) `####` is correctly NOT reserved: it is accepted and `doc show` returns it verbatim as the notes slot — the schema-keyed leaf boundary behaving as M49 specified, not a leak.
Degenerate ids: `jigc task discard ""` -> exit 1 `work-unit.malformed-id`, and `ls .jigc/tasks` still lists the directory (M50's fix holds). Mid-merge, `jigc milestone create ""` refuses on posture first (exit 1) rather than minting.
Non-git directory: `cd $(mktemp -d); jigc validate` and `jigc start` both exit 1 with the single 'not inside a git repository (no `.git` found from …) — run jigc from inside the target git repository; if this project isn't one yet, `git init` here first'.

scenarios.name: The *.commit-rejected state-truth clause contradicts the conflict finding printed beside it (FINDING 2)
scenarios.detail:
FINDING 2 — MEDIUM. `RejectionFrame::survived` is a per-door CONSTANT string composed BEFORE the rollback runs; M52's own new `<door>.rollback-conflict` / `<door>.foreign-bytes` findings are exactly the outcomes in which the rollback did not do what that constant asserts. The two then print inside ONE document, contradicting each other, and in one cell the frame's re-run instruction is falsified by the finding two lines below it.

REPRO A (false 'nothing survives') — `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`; hook that appends to docs/milestone-records/*.md and exits 1; `jigc milestone create 'Text Arm Probe'`.
OBSERVED (text arm, exit 1):
  nothing was committed — the record write and the milestone workbench were both rolled back, so nothing of milestone:text-arm-probe survives. …
  blocking · milestone.rollback-conflict — `docs/milestone-records/text-arm-probe.md` changed while this milestone-op was running, so the rollback did not restore it …
  route: … the rollback would have deleted the copy jigc created — it did not. Remove it by hand if you do not want it
  $ ls docs/milestone-records/   ->  text-arm-probe.md      <-- the file the first clause says does not exist

REPRO B (false 'is unchanged', and the re-run the frame prints cannot run) — same rig; `jigc milestone create 'Wave One'`; hook that does `for d in .jigc/tasks/*/; do mkdir -p "$d/docs" && printf 'THIRD PARTY PROSE\n' > "$d/docs/RACER.md"; done; exit 1`; `jigc milestone add-task wave-one 'sub one' --workflow dev-task --format json`.
OBSERVED (exit 1, one document on stderr):
  finding 1 route: "nothing was committed — the record append and the sub-task mint were both rolled back, so milestone:wave-one is unchanged. Fix the hook's complaint, then re-run `jigc milestone add-task wave-one 'sub one' --workflow dev-task`."
  finding 2 (`milestone.foreign-bytes`, target `.jigc/tasks/sub-one`): "…the working area this call minted was left standing rather than removed…" route: "…until that path is gone, the identical re-run blocks on the id this call already minted"
  $ cat .jigc/tasks/sub-one/docs/RACER.md -> THIRD PARTY PROSE
So 'is unchanged' is false (the mint's workbench stands) AND the re-run finding 1 tells the caller to run is the one finding 2 says will block.

HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: `grep -rn 'RejectionFrame {' crates/cli/src/*.rs` -> 7 construction sites (cli.rs:1122, migrate_corpus.rs:315, milestone.rs:554 [covering 4 match arms of `MilestoneCommand::rejection_frame`, milestone.rs:475-553], milestone.rs:5184, milestone.rs:5290, task.rs:651, task.rs:3024) = 10 distinct `survived` clauses. I drove FOUR of them: milestone create (FALSE), milestone add-task (FALSE), task finalize (TRUE — 'task call-two is intact … your task's staged docs are still in .jigc/tasks/call-two/docs/' is accurate under `finalize.rollback-conflict`), rename (TRUE-but-silent — 'so `adr:alpha-call` still holds its original identity' is true; it simply says nothing about the new path the conflict finding reports). The remaining SIX clauses (milestone add-from-spec, milestone discard, the two milestone-finalize arms, task discard, migrate-corpus) are UN-DRIVEN. So: class mechanism identified and named (a constant state-truth clause vs a runtime rollback outcome), 4 of 10 sites driven, 2 false — the other 6 are NOT bounded. Note cli.rs:1127-1135 carries a doc-comment asserting '`rollback_rename` restores the store byte-and-record identical on every pre-commit failure, hook or not, so one clause is true of both', which M52 Increment 5's own `rename.rollback-conflict` exists to contradict.

scenarios.name: command-output-contract.md's store.* keying sentence is false at three doors (FINDING 3)
scenarios.detail:
FINDING 3 — MEDIUM, and it is a law-1 break on a document 1.0.0 pins. design/command-output-contract.md:292 (a sentence M52 itself amended — it adds 'and since M52 `store.fixed-identity`') states: "`store.malformed-slug` … flattens at every one of its producers, while its `store.*` siblings — `store.not-found`, `store.no-such-leaf`, `store.unknown-type`, and since M52 `store.fixed-identity` — are keyed." Driven, two of those four named siblings are FLATTENED into the `{error}` arm at three doors, so `(code, target)` does not resolve for a driver there.

REPRO (`rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`):
  $ jigc relocate bogus --from notes --format json
  {"error": "blocking · store.unknown-type — unknown doctype `bogus`\n  at: bogus\n  route: list the available doctypes with `jigc describe`"}      exit 1
  $ jigc migrate notes/x.md --as bogus --format json
  {"error": "blocking · store.unknown-type — unknown doctype `bogus`; migratable doctypes: …\n  at: bogus\n  route: …"}                                   exit 1
  $ jigc rename bogus:x --to Y --format json
  {"error": "blocking · store.unknown-type — unknown doctype `bogus`\n  at: bogus\n  route: …"}                                                        exit 1
  $ jigc rename adr:nosuch --to X --format json
  {"error": "blocking · store.not-found — no managed doc `adr:nosuch` to rename (expected at docs/decisions/nosuch.md)\n  at: adr:nosuch\n  route: …"}   exit 1
AGAINST the keyed doors, same corpus:
  $ jigc doc show bogus:x --format json   -> findings arm, "key": {"code": "store.unknown-type", "target": "bogus:x"}
  $ jigc doc schema bogus --format json   -> findings arm, "key": {"code": "store.unknown-type", "target": "bogus"}
  $ jigc doc show adr:nosuch --format json-> findings arm, "key": {"code": "store.not-found", "target": "adr:nosuch"}
  $ jigc milestone add-from-spec m bogus:x --format json -> findings arm
One code, two wire shapes — the shape M51 Increment 6 closed for `work-unit.malformed-id` across 25 doors, still open for these.

The two locked docs also disagree with each other: design/write-commands.md:139 records for `jigc rename` a "Declared bound, inherited not introduced: these refusals reach `--format json` inside the `{\"error\": …}` envelope rather than as the structured finding projection" — which is precisely what command-output-contract.md:292 denies. And crates/cli/src/render.rs's own doc-comment above `finding_error` states the governing rule: flattening "is the right posture for a code the contract lists under no target form, and the wrong one for a code it lists under one" — `store.unknown-type` and `store.not-found` demonstrably project a target form at the keyed doors, so these three doors owe `envelope_finding_error`.

HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: the sentence names 4 codes; I drove 2 of the 4 at a flattening door and both falsify it (`store.no-such-leaf` and `store.fixed-identity` un-driven at a flattening door). Doors reached: 3 (`relocate`, `migrate --as`, `rename`). The arm is decided by whether a door wraps with `finding_error` (flat) or `envelope_finding_error` (keyed); `grep -rn 'finding_error(' crates/cli/src/ crates/engine/src/` -> 39 call sites across 12 files (task.rs 16, milestone.rs 4, start.rs 3, rename.rs 3, migrate.rs 3, cli.rs 3, render.rs 2, relocate.rs 2, repo.rs/doc.rs/describe.rs/config.rs 1 each), which I did NOT classify arm-by-arm. So: 4 (code, door) cells confirmed false; the full class is NOT enumerated.

scenarios.name: jigc relocate answers six user-reachable refusals with no code and no route line (FINDING 4)
scenarios.detail:
FINDING 4 — LOW. `jigc relocate` is a user-facing verb whose refusals mostly carry no finding identity: no `blocking · <code>` prefix, no `route:` line, and on `--format json` a bare `{error}` string a driver cannot key on.

REPRO (`rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"`):
  $ jigc relocate adr --from notes                       exit 1
  `adr` is a frozen doctype — relocate it through the version-gated `jigc migrate-corpus`, not the freeze-exempt path
  $ jigc relocate adr --from notes --format json          exit 1
  {"error": "`adr` is a frozen doctype — relocate it through the version-gated `jigc migrate-corpus`, not the freeze-exempt path"}
  $ jigc relocate adr --from '' --format json             exit 1
  {"error": "`--from` (the prior home) is required"}
Compare the two cells Increment 8 DID give codes to, in the same door:
  $ jigc relocate adr --from .jigc     -> exit 1, `blocking · config.workbench-root` with a `route:` line
  $ jigc relocate adr --from .claude   -> exit 1, `blocking · config.unusable-root` with a `route:` line

HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: `grep -n 'bail!\|anyhow!' crates/cli/src/relocate.rs` -> 7 hits. One (:284) is the codeful `render::finding_error(&finding)` path Increment 8 added for the two installed-root cells, leaving SIX code-less refusals: :75 untrackable destination, :281 `--from` required, :289 `--from` is not a valid prior home, :384 frozen doctype, :392 transient (home-less) doctype, :576 destination occupied by a managed instance. Every one is reachable from the CLI; the frozen-doctype one at :384 is the universal answer for every doctype either shipped pack resolves.

CONTEXT (so this is graded honestly, not inflated): design/corpus-migration.md:73-85 declares the door's success domain EMPTY on a stock corpus ('no doctype a stock installation resolves is freeze-exempt, so `jigc relocate` refuses every one of them at the frozen-manifest gate'), and the two root cells deliberately reuse the sibling door's codes rather than minting. So these six are a pre-existing, un-swept remainder at a door M52 opened and partially swept — INSTANCE-COUNTED FROM ONE GREP, class beyond this file UNBOUNDED. Also worth flagging as a record-vs-binary mismatch: the roadmap's Increment 8 *Proves* line says "`relocate adr --from notes` over `notes/My Note.md` refuses `ingest.unaddressable-identity`'s code"; driven on this binary it refuses at the frozen gate instead, with no code at all.

scenarios.name: schema-conformance.orphaned-instance never names migrate-corpus when the cause is a home-moving bump (FINDING 5)
scenarios.detail:
FINDING 5 — LOW (route quality, not a dead end). When a still-resolving doctype's home moves within `orphan::Territory`, the stranded below-version instance is correctly caught by `schema-conformance.orphaned-instance` at exit 1 — but the finding asserts 'no resolved doctype claims this path' and routes only at `jigc ingest` / `jigc unmanage` / 're-add the pack that defines its type', none of which is the actual one-command answer (`jigc migrate-corpus`), and all of which mis-describe the state: the doctype DOES resolve and the doc IS migratable.

REPRO (continuing the Arm 4a rig; see Finding 1's repro for the manufacture recipe, here applied to `adr`: snapshot v2, `location: decisions/` -> `location: decisions2/`, manifest 2 -> 3, re-pin):
  $ jigc doc list
  id  path  state
  (none)  docs/decisions/first-call.md  orphaned
  $ jigc validate                                                      exit 1
  blocking · schema-conformance.orphaned-instance — committed doc `docs/decisions/first-call.md` sits at a jigc-managed home and carries a `schema-version:` stamp, but no resolved doctype claims this path — its type may be defined by nothing in the composed set, or defined and homed elsewhere
    route: ask `jigc ingest`, which re-reads the file: where a resolved doctype's schema accepts it, that door names the home to move it to. …
  $ jigc migrate-corpus --dry-run
  1 would migrate, 0 already current, 0 blocked / would migrate docs/decisions2/first-call.md      <-- the real answer, named nowhere in the route
  $ jigc ingest                                                        exit 0 (the route, followed)
  needs-reconcile docs/decisions/first-call.md → adr
    blocking · ingest.wrong-location — … route: move docs/decisions/first-call.md into docs/decisions2/, then re-run `jigc ingest`
So the route is followable and eventually converges (a hand `git mv` then `migrate-corpus` for the stamp), but it costs two hops and its first sentence is false about the state. 'defined and homed elsewhere' is the clause that is true here, and the route never acts on it.

HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: instance, unbounded. One producer (`cli::orphan`'s `orphaned-instance`), one cause-discrimination it does not make; I did not enumerate the producer's other cause arms.

summary: M52's tier-0 loss classes all HOLD under adversarial driving of the real binary (target/debug/jigc @ 26d021de, 1.0.0-rc.15) in throwaway mktemp-d rigs: every rollback population kept the racer's bytes and emitted exactly one JSON document on stderr with stdout empty; all twelve un-concluded git states refused at every acting door with routes that a real shell ran and git accepted; every destroying door answered for foreign bytes through its own disposition (including collision-safe displacement — a second run of the same task id landed at NOTES.md.2 rather than clobbering the first agent's prose) with zero false fire over jigc's own files; the fixed-identity predicate refused at all eight address doors for all five derived doctypes at contract-version 7; 40 of 41 clap leaves answered each pre-dispatch fault with one parseable document; all 14 verb-routed workflows refused at both compose doors minting nothing; and the fan-out drove byte-identically across three divergent execution orders. The reds are all tier-2/tier-3 and none is data loss. The blocking one is FINDING 1: after a schema bump that also moves a doctype's home off a repo-root placement file, `jigc validate` prints "no findings — the committed store validates clean" at exit 0 and `jigc doc list` says "no committed docs" over an unmigrated below-version managed doc that `jigc migrate-corpus --dry-run` sees in the same corpus — the M42 false-green class reopened on the verb MIGRATING.md tells adopters to gate CI on, through the one axis Increment 7 widened on the migrate side only. Three smaller law-1 breaks follow the wave's own third claim-clause: a `*.commit-rejected` frame whose constant state-truth clause is falsified by the conflict finding printed two lines below it (2 of 4 driven sites false, 6 sites un-driven), `command-output-contract.md:292`'s claim that the `store.*` siblings "are keyed" falsified at three flattening doors, and six code-less refusals at `jigc relocate`. HONEST BOUND, stated so triage does not mistake this verdict: the fan-out green is an N-PROCESS BINARY SIM plus the adapter spawn template rendered through the binary and executed verbatim — the genuine concurrent assistant Task-tool spawn is the orchestrator's main-session artifact, which I am headless and did NOT run.
